items.b: GOLD BREAKS $4,550 IN BEIJING AND ADDS $47.96 MORE BY NEW YORK
items.t: Eastmoney timestamped spot gold at $4,554.441 at 14:51 Beijing on 21 August, up 0.8%. Friday's last New York print, this paper's mark of record, is $4,602.40. Same session, ten hours apart. Drivers named: a repo expansion from $20bn to $40bn, falling long-end yields and US debt past $40 trillion.

items.b: THE EDITOR RE-READ THE TAPE AT PRESS TIME AND WROTE NOTHING BACK
items.t: Saturday has no spot session. Kitco returned Friday's last print unchanged at gold $4,602.40 and silver $68.86, so the 05:00 marks stand. Gold is up $20.80 or 0.45% on this paper's 21 August mark; silver is down $0.45 or 0.65%, the only metal lower.

items.b: PLATINUM AND PALLADIUM STAY HELD ON A TWO-PAGE GAP OF 1.00% AND 1.47%
items.t: Kitco read $1,877.00 and $1,331.00 at press time, TradingEconomics $1,895.70 and $1,350.50. Both gaps are outside the band gold and silver cleared at 0.11%, so the last agreed marks of $1,881.00 and $1,336.00 carry unch. Both held marks sit inside today's live range.

items.b: CHOW SANG SANG'S COUNTER HAS ADDED 80 YUAN A GRAM IN THIRTEEN DAYS
items.t: Eastmoney carries the brand's pure gold jewellery at 1,365 yuan a gram, up 6 after 46 the day before. This paper recorded the same counter at 1,285 yuan on 8 August. That is 6.23% passed through to the Chinese shopper in under a fortnight.

items.b: INDIA'S JULY GOLD IMPORTS MORE THAN DOUBLE TO $4.16 BILLION
items.t: The World Gold Council puts July at $4.16bn against June's $1.97bn, with volumes at 40 to 45 tonnes against 20 and MCX turning over 14.9 tonnes a day. The ETF leg went the other way: net inflows of INR15.6bn, 55% lower month on month.

items.b: THREE GOOD DELIVERY NOTICES IN SEVENTEEN DAYS, ALL OF THEM CHINESE
items.t: Shandong Gold Smelting came off both LBMA lists on 5 August after a US forced-labour entity listing. Shenzhen Zhonghenglong joined the gold list on 17 August. Hunan Shuikoushan came off the silver list on 21 August after a modified assurance opinion. Neither suspension concerns a failed assay.

items.b: YORAM DVASH TAKES THE CHAIR AT THE COMPANY THAT SELLS 30% OF DEBSWANA
items.t: Okavango Diamond Company named the former WFDB president board chairman, reported 20 August, filling a seat empty since November. Under the February 2025 sales agreement ODC takes 30% of Debswana's rough for five years and 40% for the next five. No figures accompanied the announcement.

items.b: VASANT MEHTA, GJEPC CHAIRMAN FROM 2008 TO 2010, HAS DIED AT 81
items.t: He was the council's vice chairman in 1991-92 and again in 2006-08, and convened its banking, insurance and taxation committee for years afterwards. He represented India at the World Diamond Council, WFDB, IDMA, CIBJO and the Kimberley Process.

items.b: MINISO GROWS 53% AND TAKES THE TOP OF NRF'S HOT 25
items.t: Kantar's ranking of US domestic sales growth from 2024 to 2025 puts Miniso first, Dick's Sporting Goods second at 49% after buying Foot Locker, then Daiso at 26%, Primark at 24% and Five Below at 23%. Every name in the top five is a value format.
